text.p: Retail and services group Vendex on Tuesday dismissed speculation it was poised for a takeover in the services sector, saying it had no immediate plans to spend the proceeds from the sale of its stake in store chain KBB.
"The decision to spin off Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer should not be taken to mean Vendex is looking to finance an imminent takeover," a Vendex spokesman said.
Vendex said earlier it had decided to sell its 36 percent stake in KBB as it no longer saw its stake in the Dutch department store chain as a strategic investment.

Vendex's announcement propelled the stock to an intra-day high of 73.80 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, up from Monday's close of 71.80. The shares later fell back to trade up 80 cents at 72.60.
Dealers said the share price rally was fuelled by speculation the group was looking to cash in its stake to finance a takeover in the business services sector.
"Some market sources have named (U.S. temporary employment group) Kelly, but BIS of France is a more likely candidate," one said.
Vendex acquired BIS Propriete, a cleaning subsidiary of the French firm, midway through last year.
Another dealer confirmed the market talk of a business services takeover but added he had heard Vendex could also be eyeing an acquisition in the supermarket sector.
But the Vendex spokesman said no immediate deals were on the cards, although proceeds from the KBB sale would be used to finance further expansion.
"Our strategy is to become a European player in cleaning and temporary employment services and to further bolster our position in the food retail business," the spokesman said.

Vendex has declined to put a price on its stake in KBB, but market sources calculate that its holding of some 4.25 million shares will raise about 620 million guilders, based on KBB's closing share price of 146.20 guilders on Monday.
KBB's share price was badly hit by the news, falling 6.50 guilders to 139.70 in late Tuesday trade.

Vendex said its KBB shareholding would be sold in an international placement carried out by a syndicate led by Morgan Stanley and further including ABN AMRO Rothschild, ING Barings and UBS. The placement was expected to be completed within two weeks, the spokesman said.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
